transcript.content: Hi, welcome in—I'm Dr. [Name]. What brings you in to see me today?

Hello. Um... I guess I'm here because... well, things have just been feeling kind of flat lately. Just... heavy. 

The things that usually make me feel like myself, like going on my photography walks, or mentoring the kids... even just keeping a clean calendar. I don't know. I just stopped initiating them.
How long have you been feeling this way—flat and heavy, with less interest in your usual activities?

Um... it's been a while. Maybe... a year and three months? Give or take. 

It started around the time... well, a family member of mine had some health issues. Their behavior was changing, and... I just had to step in and take on coordinating everything for them. So... yeah. Since around then.

Over this past year and three months, has this low, heavy feeling been present pretty much every day without a break, or have there been stretches—days or weeks—where your mood actually returned to normal in between?
Um... I don't really know. It's hard to keep track of every single day over a year. It's just... it's just been heavy. I haven't really noticed if there were breaks.
During this time, have you had thoughts of worthlessness, excessive guilt, or thoughts about death or hurting yourself?
Um... no. Not really. I haven't... I don't think about hurting myself or anything like that. It's just... like I said, just heavy. That's all.
Besides feeling flat and heavy, have you noticed changes in your sleep, appetite, energy, or ability to concentrate during this time?

Um... I don't know. Sleep is... sleep is just sleep, I guess. I haven't really been paying attention to my appetite. Energy's just... low. Like I said, it's just heavy. I just try to get through the day.
Before this past year and three months, had you ever gone through a similar period of feeling this low or 'heavy' for weeks at a time?
Um... I don't really think so. I don't remember feeling quite like this before. It's mostly just been... recently.
Have you noticed it's been harder than usual to concentrate, focus, or make everyday decisions during this time?
Um... no. Not really. I just... I do my work and that's it. I haven't really noticed a difference.
During this past year and three months, have you often felt hopeless about things or found yourself doubting your own self-worth or abilities?
Um... no. Not really. I don't... I don't really sit around thinking about that kind of stuff. I just go to work and do my job.
Have you noticed any change in your appetite during this time—either eating much more than usual or having little to no appetite?
Um... no, not really. I eat about the same, I guess. I haven't really paid attention to it.
Is that family member's health situation and your role in coordinating their care still ongoing right now, or has that situation been resolved or improved?
Um... yeah, it's still ongoing. She's still... you know, she still needs help. So I'm still doing it.
Do you notice your mood lifting even briefly on days when you get a break from the caregiving responsibilities, or does the heavy feeling stay the same no matter what's happening with that situation?
Um... I don't really know. I don't really keep track of my mood like that. I guess it just... stays about the same. I haven't really noticed a difference.

However, the symptom burden does not meet full criteria for a Major Depressive Episode—patient explicitly denies worthlessness/guilt, denies concentration difficulty, denies appetite change, denies sleep disturbance, and denies suicidal ideation.
